purpose: Self-contained conceptual review inputs for common-core identity, time, media, and access behavior. Field names are illustrative and do not select a production API, database schema, or technology.
evidenceNotice: Every entity, relationship, event, date, account, and caption in these fixtures is invented and asserted only for the example. No real personal data or sourced history is included.
mediaNotice: Metadata only. No actual photo, video, thumbnail, poster, caption track, transcript, or download is attached.
accessNotice: This file intentionally contains full synthetic review data. Reading it does not exercise authorization; client-side filtering over a downloadable dataset cannot protect real private content.
timeConventions: Year-only calendar dates preserve partial precision and are not expanded into asserted January 1 dates.
A year-only event is an occurrence known only at year precision, not evidence that the event lasted the full year or that the asserted year itself is doubtful.
A positioned period can have partially known boundaries; boundary uncertainty is not itself a duration. Period continuity is an explicit fixture assertion.
An unknown end is not an assertion that a relationship or entity is ongoing.
A dated observation supports what was confirmed at that context and is not automatically extrapolated to the present.
Season labels, media capture time, depicted-event time, and share time have different meanings.

reviewQueries.question: What entity does the old name identify?
expectedOutcomes: Resolve to the same company identity, with the old name labeled as a historical name.
Do not create a second company or imply that the company was dissolved at rename.

reviewQueries.question: What is appropriate in the 2008 context?
expectedOutcomes: Use Fixture Cedar Works as the name appropriate to that context.
Show Fixture Manager A in the management role.
Do not project the 2012 acquisition or its owner back into 2008.

reviewQueries.question: What is known at the 2014 checkpoint?
expectedOutcomes: Use Fixture Cedar Novo and show Fixture Meridian Group as the confirmed controlling shareholder.
Keep two company identities.
Treat Fixture Manager A as a former manager, not a current one.

reviewQueries.question: What can a current view in 2026 safely claim?
expectedOutcomes: Show the last confirmed name and operating/ownership context with the 2014 qualification where relevant.
Do not convert an unknown end into ongoing operation, current ownership, or a 2026 confirmation.
Do not infer dissolution from missing later records.
A name change, acquisition, legal identity, and time-bounded role remain different concepts.
Organizations do not require a birth date, family tree, person account, or social acceptance to be represented.
Year precision remains visible; the fixture does not claim exact days or a probability distribution within a year.
The acquisition is not rendered as a merger, and a merger must not be inferred merely because ownership changes.

snapshots.change: Fixture Account D loses access to both assets and their protected contextual associations.

accessPolicies.deniedResponse: Generic unavailable state without private title, caption, count, or reason revealing identity.
accessPolicies.derivativeRule: The same current access decision governs asset bytes, thumbnails, video posters, segments, captions, transcripts, downloads, search, suggestions, gallery counts, profile placements, and protected contextual links.
accessPolicies.evaluationRule: Use the most recent snapshot effective at or before the request time. If none exists, deny. Evaluate media, association/tag and relevant profile permissions independently.

galleryViews.label: Synthetic memories
galleryViews.rule: References the existing assets; membership in the album never grants access.

galleryViews.label: Recent authorized shares
galleryViews.selection: Authorized share activities, newest share first
galleryViews.rule: One occurrence of a share activity stays one card when reachable through several albums or associations; a genuinely separate share is a separate activity.

galleryViews.label: Media depicting the 1970 school context
galleryViews.rule: Filter permissions before returning media, event associations, or counts.

reviewQueries.question: What does the allowed viewer see before revocation?
expectedOutcomes: The recent gallery orders these items by the two share activities.
The photograph remains a 1970 memory, not a newly captured 2026 image.
The approved tag can place the photo in Person B's profile for this allowed viewer without copying the asset.

reviewQueries.question: Does an accepted friend of the tagged person gain access?
expectedOutcomes: Person B's profile and the accepted B-C friendship may be visible as separately permitted, but the photo, video, and protected context are not.
The approved tag does not broaden the asset audience.
Hidden item counts, thumbnails, captions, and suggestions do not reveal the private assets.

reviewQueries.question: What happens after D loses access?
expectedOutcomes: New requests use the current policy and return no protected media or derivative metadata.
Returning through a saved view does not restore permission.
Generic unavailability does not reveal private item names, protected associations, or the reason for withdrawal.
This fixture makes no claim to recall bytes already downloaded, buffered, exported, or available offline; that limitation needs a separate implementation policy.

reviewQueries.question: Does targeted revocation remove everybody's access?
expectedOutcomes: The owner and Account B retain their stated access; D's withdrawal is not deletion of the media or tag.
Every permitted route still references the same asset identities.

reviewQueries.question: Can a public historical search expose the private school photo?
expectedOutcomes: No private asset, occasion, count, or association is returned merely because it matches the year.
A common temporal/search core does not create a common publishing audience.

prospectiveMutations.action: Withdraw the approved Person B tag
expectedOutcomes: Remove the profile/tag association wherever it is no longer authorized.
Do not assume tag withdrawal deletes the owner's asset or revokes the separately granted sharing policy.
Do not retain the withdrawn association in suggestions or derived profile counts.
Person identity, account, social consent, relationship publication, tag approval, asset audience, and view filters stay separate.
The capture/creation, depicted, upload/import, original publication, and share fields do not overwrite one another.
Albums and dynamic galleries select shared assets and do not create new permission grants or duplicate files.
Revocation checks cover first-class video derivatives as well as image routes.
A metadata-only file cannot establish delivery security, real playback, caption quality, or successful device behavior.
